So it is an EER-based threshold (with a minimum operating-hours filter), not a power-factor threshold.

The ranking is calculated among only the poor-energy robots (those that pass the inefficiency filter), not among all robots before filtering. For each application type, the aggregate representing the group is the maximum EER rank (i.e., the worst rank within that application type), reported alongside the average EER.

WITH energy AS (
    SELECT effectivenessrobot AS robot_id, SUM(energyusekwhval) AS total_energy
    FROM performance_and_safety
    GROUP BY effectivenessrobot
), hours AS (
    SELECT operbotdetref AS robot_id, MAX(totopshrval) AS toh
    FROM operation
    GROUP BY operbotdetref
), applications AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT operbotdetref AS robot_id, apptypeval
    FROM operation
), poor AS (
    SELECT a.apptypeval, e.total_energy / NULLIF(h.toh, 0) AS eer
    FROM energy e
    JOIN hours h USING (robot_id)
    JOIN applications a USING (robot_id)
    WHERE h.toh > 1000
      AND e.total_energy / NULLIF(h.toh, 0) > 0.01
), ranked AS (
    SELECT apptypeval, eer,
           PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY apptypeval ORDER BY eer DESC) AS eer_rank
    FROM poor
)
SELECT apptypeval, AVG(eer) AS avg_eer, MAX(eer_rank) AS least_efficient_rank
FROM ranked
GROUP BY apptypeval
ORDER BY avg_eer DESC
LIMIT 100;
